research_rationale: EO 13927 (signed 2020-06-04, 85 FR 35165-35170), read in full from the held FR text, directs agencies to speed infrastructure and recovery actions during the COVID-19 national emergency: transportation, Army civil works and Federal-lands projects (secs. 3-5), NEPA, ESA and Clean Water Act emergency procedures (secs. 6-8), other emergency authorities (sec. 9) and general provisions (sec. 10). Most operative sections set a 30-day report and then status reports 'at least every 30 days for the duration of the national emergency'. The machine own-term kinds (condition, emergency_duration, fixed_term, report_deadline) are not ends: 30-day periods are deadlines, and the emergency-duration wording would end the recurring reports only when the emergency ended, which was after 2021-01-20 (no held source records an earlier end). The order has no sunset or termination clause. No clause's first end needs a report date, so the order is not blocked on the report-deadline question. EO 13990 (86 FR 7037-7043, read in full; reading record scale/readings/LSP-EO_13990.json) sec. 7(a) revokes it, effective on signing, 2021-01-20; the U.S. Code note to 5 U.S.C. 601 says the same (86 FR 7041). The dossier lists no missing provision; a by-number scan of all 6,652 held FR-original texts finds EO 13927 named only in EO 13990. EO 14148 and EO 14154 (2025) revoke EO 13990 but name none of the six orders and reinstate nothing. Inventory correction: the dossier splits the tail of sec. 8(c) into a separate fragment clause 'sec8-a' ('(a)(i). Such status reports shall thereafter be provided...'); inventory_overrides merge it into sec8-c. All other spans are copied unchanged, so 44 clauses cover the operative text from sec. 1 through sec. 10(c) with no gap or overlap.
